title: Rigidified line groupoids and canonical pullback
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme and $B,X$ algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $e:B\to X$. Use their canonical small etale module categories, tensor inverse images, adjunction units and chart tensors [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Use the canonical tensor composition comparisons, characterized on pure tensors, of [def-sfb-space-module-tensor-composition]; their composites with equality of composite maps give the square comparisons. The groupoid $\mathrm{RigLine}(e)$ has objects $(L,\rho)$, where $L$ is a line module on $X$ and $\rho:e^*L\simeq\mathcal O_B$. Its morphisms are module isomorphisms $v:L\simeq M$ such that $e^*v$ followed by the rigidification of $M$ equals the rigidification of $L$.
For any commuting square $a:B'\to B$, $b:X'\to X$, $e':B'\to X'$ with $ea=be'$, define pullback by $(L,\rho)\mapsto(b^*L,e'^*b^*L\simeq a^*e^*L\xrightarrow{a^*\rho}a^*\mathcal O_B\simeq\mathcal O_{B'})$ and by $b^*$ on isomorphisms. The last unit comparison is uniquely characterized on chart tensors by $b\otimes r\mapsto b f^\sharp(r)$, and tensor pullback preserves line modules. Forgetting to the underlying module is a functor. For two successive commuting section squares in each direction of a commutative square, the two iterated pullback functors admit a unique natural isomorphism whose underlying module map is the first tensor composition comparison, the equality of the two composite space maps, and the inverse of the second tensor composition comparison. These comparisons respect rigidifications and successive squares.
